column2: Case name
column12: Issue in one line
column13: Holding in one line

column2: Madras Bar Association v. Union of India
column12: Whether the Tribunals Reforms Act, 2021 could re-enact provisions previously invalidated by the Court.
column13: invalidated key restrictions and held that legislation cannot simply override a judgment without curing the constitutional defect.

column2: Ashwini Kumar Upadhyay v. Union of India (hate speech)
column12: Whether courts may create or expand criminal offences through directions where legislation does not do so.
column13: declined the requested intervention, treating creation of criminal offences and punishments as a legislative function.

column2: Supriyo @ Supriya Chakraborty v. Union of India
column12: Whether the Court could extend marriage recognition under the Special Marriage Act to same-sex couples.
column13: left creation of a new marriage or civil-union framework to legislative policy.

column2: Ashwini Kumar Upadhyay v. Union of India (minimum age of marriage)
column12: Whether the minimum age of marriage for women should be raised to 21 to match that for men.
column13: declined to direct Parliament to establish a uniform minimum age.

column2: Sanjay Prakash v. Union of India (CAPF, OGAS)
column12: Whether executive service and promotion policies in the CAPFs complied with constitutional requirements.
column13: used judicial review to address restrictions affecting service equality and highlighted limits on executive action.

column2: Gujarat Urja Vikas Nigam Limited v. Amit Gupta
column12: How the IBC tribunal's jurisdiction applies to disputes involving contracts and regulatory matters.
column13: clarifying jurisdictional boundaries among tribunals, contracts, and courts.

column2: In Re: Special Reference No. 1 of 2025 (Governors, Articles 200 and 201)
column12: What limits govern a Governor's options when considering State bills.
column13: described limits on gubernatorial inaction and addressed the relationship between executive and legislative roles.

column2: Anoop Baranwal v. Union of India
column12: How the Chief Election Commissioner and Election Commissioners should be appointed in the absence of legislation.
column13: prescribed an interim appointment committee arrangement until Parliament enacted a law.

column2: Animal Welfare Board of India v. Union of India (Jallikattu)
column11: Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960
column12: Whether State amendments permitting Jallikattu were valid after the Court's earlier decision.
column13: upheld the amendments, treating them as changing the legal framework considered earlier.

column2: Government of NCT of Delhi v. Union of India (Services)
column12: Which government controls services in the National Capital Territory of Delhi.
column13: recognized a significant role for Delhi's elected government in administration and discussed federal boundaries.

column2: Association for Democratic Reforms v. Union of India (Electoral Bonds)
column12: Whether the Electoral Bond Scheme and related amendments were constitutionally valid.
column13: invalidated the scheme on rights grounds, while recognizing that legislation remains subject to judicial review.

column2: Cox & Kings Ltd. v. SAP India Pvt. Ltd.
column12: How the group-of-companies doctrine applies under Indian arbitration law.
column13: addressed interpretation of corporate relationships while applying the governing statutory framework.

column2: Subhash Desai v. Principal Secretary, Governor of Maharashtra
column12: Whether the Governor could call for a trust vote based on internal party disputes and how the Speaker's role applied.
column13: found the floor-test decision unlawful but declined to restore the former Chief Minister after his resignation.

column2: Neil Aurelio Nunes v. Union of India (NEET OBC/EWS)
column12: Whether the reservation policy for OBC and EWS candidates in NEET was subject to judicial intervention.
column13: upheld the policy and described limits on judicial review of policy choices.

column2: Pankaj Bansal v. Union of India
column12: What safeguards apply to arrest powers exercised by enforcement authorities under the PMLA.
column13: required written communication of the grounds of arrest as a check on executive power.

column2: Central Electricity Regulatory Commission v. NTPC
column12: How far courts may intervene in tariff decisions made by expert regulatory bodies.
column13: emphasized deference to technical expertise and cautioned against courts setting tariffs.

column2: S. G. Vombatkere v. Union of India (Sedition)
column12: How Section 124A of the Indian Penal Code should be treated while its constitutionality was challenged.
column13: stayed enforcement temporarily and asked the Union to reconsider the provision.

column2: State of Punjab v. Principal Secretary to Governor
column12: Whether the Governor could question the validity of an Assembly session when considering bills passed by it.
column13: held that the Governor could not question the session's validity and stressed the functioning of the elected legislature.

column2: In Re: Section 6A of the Citizenship Act
column12: Whether Parliament had competence to enact Section 6A and whether the provision was constitutional.
column13: upheld Section 6A and recognized Parliament's latitude in citizenship matters.
